beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! Ready for some more logic fun?
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, you became a logic detective. You learned that a statement is either true, or false. A week has seven days? True! All birds can fly? False, because of penguins!
beats.caption: Last time: every statement is true or false

beats.vo: Today is chapter two of Logic and Reasoning. And it's all about three tiny words. The word and. The word or. And the word not.
beats.caption: Chapter 2 · AND, OR, NOT

beats.vo: They look small, right? But these little words help computers, and games, make big decisions, every single second.
beats.caption: Tiny words → big decisions

beats.vo: And to learn them, we're going to a birthday party! Let's go.
beats.caption: Let's go to a birthday party!

beats.vo: It's Anaya's birthday party! And guess who's guarding the door? Robo, our robot friend! He checks every guest, before they come in.
beats.caption: Robo guards the door at Anaya's party

beats.vo: Anaya gives Robo one rule. Bring cake and juice. A rule is a check that gives a yes, or a no. Yes, come in. Or no, sorry.
beats.caption: Rule: bring cake AND juice

beats.vo: Ding dong! Here comes Arjun. He's carrying a big chocolate cake. Yum. But, no juice.
beats.caption: Arjun brings cake… but no juice

beats.vo: So, does Robo let Arjun in? Yes, or no? Think about it.
beats.caption: Can Arjun come in? Think!

beats.vo: The answer is no. The rule says cake and juice, and that means you need both. Arjun has the cake, but the juice is missing. So Robo says, sorry!
beats.caption: No! AND needs both. Juice is missing.

beats.vo: Arjun runs home, and comes back with a juice box. Cake, and juice. Now Robo says, yes, come in!
beats.caption: Cake AND juice → Yes, come in!

beats.vo: So here's our first tiny word. The word and means both things must be true.
beats.caption: AND = both must be true

beats.vo: Let's check four guests. Cake and juice? Yes! Only cake? No. Only juice? No. And nothing at all? Definitely no.
beats.caption: Both → Yes. Anything less → No.

beats.vo: See? The word and is a little fussy. It wants everything on the list. If even one thing is missing, the answer is no.
beats.caption: AND is fussy. One missing → No!

beats.vo: Quick check. The rule is, bring a gift and a card. Kabir brings a gift, but no card. Can he come in?
beats.caption: Gift AND card. Kabir has only a gift.

beats.vo: No! He has the gift, but no card. And needs both, so Kabir has to go and make a card.
beats.caption: No. AND needs both, the card is missing

beats.vo: Now our second word. Or. Imagine the rule at the fun fair gate is, enter with a ticket, or a pass.
beats.caption: Fun fair rule: a ticket OR a pass

beats.vo: The word or means at least one thing must be true. Only a ticket? Yes! Only a pass? Yes!
beats.caption: OR = at least one must be true

beats.vo: And what if you have both, a ticket and a pass? Still yes! Two is more than enough. The word or is happy with one, or both.
beats.caption: Both? Still YES! Both is fine too.

beats.vo: It only says no when you have neither. No ticket, and no pass. Sorry!
beats.caption: Neither → No

beats.vo: Quick check. Sara has only a pass. Can she enter?
beats.caption: Sara has only a pass. Can she enter?

beats.vo: Yes! With or, one is enough, and Sara has her pass. Have fun on the big wheel, Sara!
beats.caption: Yes! For OR, one is enough

beats.vo: And our third word is not. Not means the opposite. It flips things around.
beats.caption: NOT = the opposite. It flips it!

beats.vo: Not true becomes false. And not false becomes true. Just like flipping a light switch, from on, to off.
beats.caption: NOT true = false · NOT false = true

beats.vo: Here's a rule at Nani's house. Come in only if you are not wearing muddy shoes. Clean shoes? Yes, come in. Muddy shoes? No way! Nani just cleaned the floor.
beats.caption: Rule: NOT wearing muddy shoes

beats.vo: Now Aman walks up. His shoes are clean, so they're not muddy. The rule is true, and Aman can go in!
beats.caption: Clean shoes → not muddy → Aman goes in

beats.vo: Now here's where computers come in. Video games use these little words all the time, to decide what happens.
beats.caption: Games use AND and OR to decide

beats.vo: A game might say, if you have a key and a torch, open the cave. That's an if-both rule. You need both.
beats.caption: Key AND torch → open the cave (if-both)

beats.vo: Another might say, if you find a coin or a gem, get a point. That's an if-either rule. Either one works.
beats.caption: Coin OR gem → get a point (if-either)

beats.vo: And the game checks these rules again and again, many times every second, while you play!
beats.caption: Checked many times every second!

beats.vo: Let's play! Four explorers reach the cave. Tia has only a key. Raj has only a torch. Zoya has a key and a torch. And Neel has neither. Who can open the cave? Think.
beats.caption: Key AND torch. Who can open the cave?

beats.vo: Only Zoya! The rule needs both. Tia and Raj each have just one. And Neel has nothing. Go on Zoya, open the cave!
beats.caption: Only Zoya has both the key and the torch

beats.vo: Now, a tricky one! Pooja's party rule says, bring juice or sweets, and do not come late. Pooja brings a box of sweets, and she arrives on time. Can she come in? Think it through.
beats.caption: Juice OR sweets, AND NOT late. Pooja?

beats.vo: Let's check it in parts. Part one, juice or sweets. She has sweets, and one is enough, so that part is true.
beats.caption: Part 1: juice OR sweets → true

beats.vo: Part two, do not come late. She came on time, so she's not late. True again!
beats.caption: Part 2: NOT late → true

beats.vo: Both parts are true, and the word and joins them together. So yes, Pooja can come in. Enjoy the party!
beats.caption: True AND true → Yes, Pooja comes in!

beats.vo: Okay champ, here's a practice check, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: You need a hat and a ticket to enter. You have only a ticket. Can you enter? Pause the video, and say your answer out loud.
beats.caption: Hat AND ticket. You have only a ticket.

beats.vo: No, you can't. The rule needs both, and you're missing the hat. Grab a hat, then come back! Did you get it? Brilliant!
beats.caption: No! AND needs both. Grab a hat!

beats.vo: Let's remember what we learned today. The word and, means both must be true.
beats.caption: AND → both must be true

beats.vo: The word or, means at least one is true. And both is fine too.
beats.caption: OR → at least one is true

beats.vo: The word not, flips it to the opposite. Not true is false.
beats.caption: NOT → flip it to the opposite

beats.vo: And games use if-both, and if-either rules, to decide what happens.
beats.caption: Games use if-both and if-either

beats.vo: Chapter two, done! You're a party-planning logic pro, champ!
beats.caption: Chapter 2 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
